in_sanskrit.name: भविनी
in_sanskrit.long_meaning:
भव- (bhav) - to be, to exist, to create + नि- (ni) - towards + ई- (i) - feminine suffix
Therefore, Bhavini means the one who creates or the one who exists towards creativity.

in_hindi.name: भविनी
in_hindi.long_meaning:
भव- (bhav) - to be, to exist + नाती (nati) - one who is
Bhavini in Hindi is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Bhavini' which means 'one who exists towards creativity' or 'one who creates'.

in_tamil.name: பவினி
in_tamil.long_meaning:
புலிகல் (puli) - tiger + கல் (kal) - strength + அவர்களுக்கு (avarkalukku) - for them + விழிக்கையில் (vizhikkaiyil) - in the midst of + வழிக்கையாள் (vazhikkaiyal) - one who helps
Bhavini in Tamil means 'the one who helps tigers in the midst of their fights'.

in_telugu.name: భవినీ

Bhavini in Telugu is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Bhavini' which means 'the dark lord who exists'.

historical_references.reference: Bhavani, also known as Bhavani Mata, is an important Hindu goddess worshipped as the mother goddess or Shakti. She is popularly known as the 'Mother of the Cosmos'. The name 'Bhavani' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'bhavah' which means 'existence', and 'ini' meaning 'mother'. She is often equated with the goddess Parvati, who is the consort of Shiva, and is considered to be the mother of Ganesha.

Bhavani is also the name of a queen mentioned in the Indian epic Mahabharata. She was the daughter of King Bhagiratha and Queen Indumati, and was the wife of King Yuddhishthira. Bhavani is known for her great hospitality and kindness towards the Pandava brothers, especially Yuddhishthira. She is also known as Draupadi, the wife of the Pandava brothers, and is revered as the embodiment of the goddess Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and prosperity.
